questions.a: AI readiness describes how well a country or business is set up to build and use AI across the whole stack. It covers talent, quality data, affordable infrastructure such as cloud and GPUs, policy that enables innovation while protecting rights, and how widely businesses are experimenting. It's a spectrum rather than a single score.

questions.q: Which Asian countries lead in AI readiness?
questions.a: Singapore and China are the front-runners. Singapore has a national AI strategy, the government-backed AI Verify testing framework and strong talent programs. China grows AI quickly through state support, national champions and a strict regulatory approach.

questions.q: Which countries are catching up in AI?
questions.a: South Korea, Japan and India are the fast followers. South Korea is investing in AI semiconductors to rely less on foreign chips, and Japan is moving quickly on generative AI in creative industries like manga and film. India's large IT workforce and digital public infrastructure position it as a global AI development hub.

questions.q: How ready is Southeast Asia for AI?
questions.a: Momentum is mixed. Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia are investing in cloud and AI training but face gaps in data infrastructure and language localization. Thailand includes AI in its Digital Economy blueprint without a central AI policy, and the Philippines is focusing on AI literacy to protect its BPO workforce.

questions.q: What does AI readiness in Asia mean for business leaders?
questions.a: Where you operate shapes how easily you can scale AI. You'll find it easier in countries with strong compute access and stable regulation, and local flagship AI projects can be worth partnering with. In markets with unclear rules, it helps to take part in shaping policy, and upskilling your team matters everywhere.
